newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank Boston seeks asset-backed offer for China co.
newsitem.headline: Bank Boston seeks asset-backed offer for China co.

text.p: Bank of Boston said on Tuesday it was expecting to receive a mandate for a bond offer in the United States backed by receivables of a major Chinese company.
It did not name the company although it said this would be seven- to eight-year debt and would be the first such transaction for a Chinese firm.
Bank of Boston officials told reporters that such offers normally would be for more than $150 million.
"We think it's the right time," said Rusell Magarity, managing director and area executive, Asia.
Bank of Boston hoped to have the offer ready in the next two months and that other such deals for securitised debt could be made in future, he said.
Magarity said the receivables would be dollar denominated or could be swapped into dollars. Chinese regulatory approval has already been obtained, he added.
Bank officials also said they expected to receive a mandate for financing linked to sales of telecommunications equipment.
Bank of Boston oficials said they had already met officials of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications for equipment for local telecommunications authorities. They gave no further details.
